13:  * Content plugins have a base path and a localized path to source content from.
14:  * We will look into the localized path in priority.
15:  */
16: export type ContentPaths = {
17:   /**
18:    * The absolute path to the base content directory, like `"<siteDir>/docs"`.
19:    */
20:   contentPath: string;
21:   /**
22:    * The absolute path to the localized content directory, like
23:    * `"<siteDir>/i18n/zh-Hans/plugin-content-docs"`.
24:    */
25:   contentPathLocalized: string;
26: };
27: 
28: /** Data structure representing each broken Markdown link to be reported. */
29: export type BrokenMarkdownLink<T extends ContentPaths> = {
30:   /** Absolute path to the file containing this link. */
31:   filePath: string;
32:   /**
33:    * This is generic because it may contain extra metadata like version name,
34:    * which the reporter can provide for context.
35:    */
36:   contentPaths: T;
37:   /**
38:    * The content of the link, like `"./brokenFile.md"`
39:    */
40:   link: string;
41: };
42: 
43: /**
44:  * Takes a Markdown file and replaces relative file references with their URL
45:  * counterparts, e.g. `[link](./intro.md)` => `[link](/docs/intro)`, preserving
46:  * everything else.
47:  *
48:  * This method uses best effort to find a matching file. The file reference can
49:  * be relative to the directory of the current file (most likely) or any of the
50:  * content paths (so `/tutorials/intro.md` can be resolved as
51:  * `<siteDir>/docs/tutorials/intro.md`). Links that contain the `http(s):` or
52:  * `@site/` prefix will always be ignored.
53:  */
54: export function replaceMarkdownLinks<T extends ContentPaths>({
55:   siteDir,
56:   fileString,
57:   filePath,
58:   contentPaths,
59:   sourceToPermalink,
60: }: {
61:   /** Absolute path to the site directory, used to resolve aliased paths. */
62:   siteDir: string;
63:   /** The Markdown file content to be processed. */
64:   fileString: string;
65:   /** Absolute path to the current file containing `fileString`. */
66:   filePath: string;
67:   /** The content paths which the file reference may live in. */
68:   contentPaths: T;
69:   /**
70:    * A map from source paths to their URLs. Source paths are `@site` aliased.
71:    */
72:   sourceToPermalink: {[aliasedPath: string]: string};
73: }): {
74:   /**
75:    * The content with all Markdown file references replaced with their URLs.
76:    * Unresolved links are left as-is.
77:    */
78:   newContent: string;
79:   /** The list of broken links,  */
80:   brokenMarkdownLinks: BrokenMarkdownLink<T>[];
81: } {
82:   const brokenMarkdownLinks: BrokenMarkdownLink<T>[] = [];
83: 
84:   // Replace internal markdown linking (except in fenced blocks).
85:   let lastCodeFence: string | null = null;
86:   const lines = fileString.split('\n').map((line) => {
87:     const codeFence = line.trimStart().match(/^`{3,}|^~{3,}/)?.[0];
88:     if (codeFence) {
89:       if (!lastCodeFence) {
90:         lastCodeFence = codeFence;
91:         // If we are in a ````-fenced block, all ``` would be plain text instead
92:         // of fences
93:       } else if (codeFence.startsWith(lastCodeFence)) {
94:         lastCodeFence = null;
95:       }
96:     }
97:     if (lastCodeFence) {
98:       return line;
99:     }
100: 
101:     let modifiedLine = line;
102:     // Replace inline-style links or reference-style links e.g:
103:     // This is [Document 1](doc1.md)
104:     // [doc1]: doc1.md
105:     const mdRegex =
106:       /(?:\]\(|\]:\s*)(?!https?:\/\/|@site\/)<?(?<filename>[^'"\]\s>]+(?:\s[^'"\]\s>]+)*\.mdx?)>?/g;
107:     let mdMatch = mdRegex.exec(modifiedLine);
108:     while (mdMatch !== null) {
109:       // Replace it to correct html link.
110:       const mdLink = mdMatch.groups!.filename!;
111: 
112:       const sourcesToTry: string[] = [];
113:       // ./file.md and ../file.md are always relative to the current file
114:       if (!mdLink.startsWith('./') && !mdLink.startsWith('../')) {
115:         sourcesToTry.push(...getContentPathList(contentPaths), siteDir);
116:       }
117:       // /file.md is always relative to the content path
118:       if (!mdLink.startsWith('/')) {
119:         sourcesToTry.push(path.dirname(filePath));
120:       }
121: 
122:       const aliasedSourceMatch = sourcesToTry
123:         .map((p) => path.join(p, decodeURIComponent(mdLink)))
124:         .map((source) => aliasedSitePath(source, siteDir))
125:         .find((source) => sourceToPermalink[source]);
126: 
127:       const permalink: string | undefined = aliasedSourceMatch
128:         ? sourceToPermalink[aliasedSourceMatch]
129:         : undefined;
130: 
131:       if (permalink) {
132:         // MDX won't be happy if the permalink contains a space, we need to
133:         // convert it to %20
134:         const encodedPermalink = permalink
135:           .split('/')
136:           .map((part) => part.replace(/\s/g, '%20'))
137:           .join('/');
138:         modifiedLine = modifiedLine.replace(
139:           mdMatch[0]!,
140:           mdMatch[0]!.replace(mdLink, encodedPermalink),
141:         );
142:         // Adjust the lastIndex to avoid passing over the next link if the
143:         // newly replaced URL is shorter.
144:         mdRegex.lastIndex += encodedPermalink.length - mdLink.length;
145:       } else {
146:         const brokenMarkdownLink: BrokenMarkdownLink<T> = {
147:           contentPaths,
148:           filePath,
149:           link: mdLink,
150:         };
151: 
152:         brokenMarkdownLinks.push(brokenMarkdownLink);
153:       }
154:       mdMatch = mdRegex.exec(modifiedLine);
155:     }
156:     return modifiedLine;
157:   });
158: 
159:   const newContent = lines.join('\n');
160: 
161:   return {newContent, brokenMarkdownLinks};
